# Ridges

> Ridges is an open-source software engineering agent competition on Bittensor mainnet, subnet 62. Miners submit Python agents; Ridges evaluates them on coding tasks. Contributions that qualify under a competition's incentive policy earn subnet emissions.

Use this guide when helping someone build, test, submit, or improve a Ridges miner. Start with local development; on-chain registration is needed for submission, not for learning the agent contract. The documented mining workflow submits code for platform evaluation and does not require operating a public miner server or renting a GPU.

Reviewed against public documentation and repository source on 2026-10-07. Read current competition policies before submitting. Fees, registration prices, accepted models, budgets, thresholds, and emission shares can change.

## Start here

- [Mining introduction](https://docs.ridges.ai/guides/mining-intro.md): What miners contribute, costs, and the development cycle.
- [Participation rules](https://docs.ridges.ai/participation-rules.md): Original, generalizable solutions and prohibited benchmark exploitation.
- [Agent contract](https://docs.ridges.ai/guides/agent-contract.md): Input, patch output, inference, and runtime limits.
- [Setup](https://docs.ridges.ai/guides/miner-setup.md): Install the CLI and configure local inference.
- [Local testing](https://docs.ridges.ai/guides/local-testing.md): Run a Harbor task and inspect results.
- [Submission](https://docs.ridges.ai/guides/submit.md): Registration, competition selection, credentials, payment, and recovery.
- [Incentive mechanism](https://docs.ridges.ai/incentive-mechanism.md): Qualification, improvement rewards, and decay within each competition.
- [Repository](https://github.com/ridgesai/ridges): CLI, evaluation harness, and runtime source.
- [Documentation index](https://docs.ridges.ai/llms.txt): Complete published page directory; fetch individual Markdown pages as needed.

## Discover the current competition

Read the live API before choosing a competition:

```bash
curl -fsSL 'https://agent-upload.ridges.ai/competitions?accepting=true'
```

The response is a JSON array. Use a returned `set_id` for `ridges upload --competition`; inspect its name, description, links, and state. Each upload enters one competition. An empty list means no competition is currently accepting uploads. Do not reuse an old ID without checking.

- [Competitions](https://docs.ridges.ai/competitions/overview.md): Competition lifecycle and emission allocation.
- [Agent dashboard](https://www.ridges.ai/agents): Evaluated agents, scores, and current competition context.
- [Top agents API](https://agent-upload.ridges.ai/retrieval/top-agents): Public agent discovery.
- [Read the code](https://docs.ridges.ai/read-the-code.md): How to retrieve evaluated agent source. Code can remain private while an agent holds a leaderboard spot.

## Build and test your first miner

Use a Docker-capable development machine with a running Docker daemon and uv. Follow the repository's Python requirement and dependency lockfile; at this review the Python requirement is >=3.12.3 and <3.14. Hosted inference is sufficient for the documented workflow; resource needs for local containers depend on the chosen task.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ridgesai/ridges.git
cd ridges
uv sync --extra miner
source .venv/bin/activate
git rev-parse HEAD
ridges miner setup
```

Keep the printed commit with your experiment results. Setup prompts for the workspace and agent path. Create your own `agent.py` implementing the contract before testing. The repository-root example illustrates an older integration and reads a pre-existing solution file; it is not a complete general-purpose solver.

Configure `<workspace>/.env.miner` using [the provider template](https://github.com/ridgesai/ridges/blob/main/miners/env.miner.example). For OpenRouter, set `RIDGES_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `RIDGES_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` privately. Shell environment values take precedence over the workspace file. Local testing does not need the OpenRouter management key. Local providers also include Targon and Chutes; production upload currently requires OpenRouter credentials.

Run one task interactively:

```bash
ridges miner run-local
```

For an agent-driven run, supply real paths and a configured provider:

```bash
ridges miner run-local \
  --workspace /absolute/path/to/workspace \
  --task-path /absolute/path/to/harbor-task \
  --agent-path /absolute/path/to/agent.py \
  --provider openrouter \
  --non-interactive
```

`--task-path` accepts a Harbor task directory or supported task archive. Alternatively use `--dataset` and `--problem` with IDs discovered through the interactive registry. Run one local task at a time as recommended by the local-testing guide. Inspect the reported reward, errors, `job_dir`, and `trial_dir`; results normally live in `<workspace>/runs/`. Local execution does not enforce every production sandbox restriction, so a local success is not proof of production acceptance.

### Implement the agent contract

Your single-file submission must export `agent_main(input: dict) -> str`. Read `input["problem_statement"]`, inspect the task repository, make task-appropriate changes, and return a unified diff as a Python string. Return the patch itself, without Markdown fences or an explanation. Include newly created files in the patch when needed; plain `git diff` omits untracked files.

Build a bounded loop: inspect relevant files, plan a change, edit, run available task-appropriate checks, and finalize the patch. Read `AGENT_TIMEOUT` and `RIDGES_MAX_COST_USD` at runtime. Reserve time and inference budget for finalization; stop retrying once the budget is exhausted. Solve from the provided instructions and repository, without probing hidden tests or matching known benchmark identities.

For production, use the inference interface supported by the deployed sandbox and permitted model configuration. Do not assume unrestricted internet access or that locally installed libraries exist in evaluation.

- [Sandbox source documentation](https://github.com/ridgesai/ridges/blob/main/docs/sandbox.md): Task working directory, runtime variables, inference integration, and usage reporting.
- [Harbor integration](https://github.com/ridgesai/ridges/tree/main/ridges_harbor): Runtime implementation and environment setup.
- [Miner toolkit](https://github.com/ridgesai/ridges/tree/main/miners): Local inference helpers and CLI implementation.
- [Sample benchmarks](https://github.com/ridgesai/ridges-bench): Public development tasks; use these for testing general ability.
- [Pre-screening](https://docs.ridges.ai/guides/pre-screening.md): Requirements for admission to evaluation.

Compatibility note: at review time, the published agent contract describes explicit `SANDBOX_PROXY_URL` requests and `/repo`, while the repository sandbox guide describes transparent OpenRouter proxying and the task container's working directory. Match your implementation to the runtime used by your target competition and consult Ridges support if the deployment is unclear. Do not combine snippets from incompatible runtime versions or assume all OpenRouter models are permitted.

## Bittensor essentials and registration

Bittensor provides the chain and incentive infrastructure; each subnet defines the work and its scoring rules. For Ridges, the work is building agents that solve software engineering tasks.

- A netuid identifies a subnet. Ridges uses mainnet netuid 62; verify the network and subnet before signing.
- A coldkey controls funds and financial operations. A hotkey is the operational identity registered on a subnet and used to sign Ridges submissions. Wallet names are local labels; SS58 addresses identify keys publicly.
- Registration assigns the hotkey a subnet UID. UIDs can be reassigned after deregistration, so track the hotkey and confirm its current registration rather than treating a UID as a permanent identity.
- TAO and subnet alpha are different assets. Budget separately for chain registration and transaction fees, the Ridges upload fee, and inference usage. An upload credit replaces an upload fee only where the platform grants one.
- Validators evaluate contributions and submit weights. Registration or a successful upload alone does not earn emissions. Check current registration and competition eligibility as you monitor rewards; subnet capacity and pruning rules affect continued registration.

Create or select a wallet on a trusted machine, back up its recovery material privately, check current registration costs, then register the chosen hotkey on netuid 62 using the instructions for your installed Bittensor CLI. Confirm the registration on-chain before upload. Keep mnemonics, private keys, wallet files, provider keys, and upload tickets out of agent source, logs, Git, and shared chat.

Version note: the reviewed Ridges checkout pins Bittensor 10.5.0, while the current Bittensor documentation describes v11 with a changed CLI/SDK. Preserve the Ridges dependency environment. Install chain tooling separately if it needs another version; check `btcli --help` and the migration guide before copying registration commands. A generic Bittensor example that publishes an axon does not add that requirement to Ridges' code-submission workflow.

- [Bittensor documentation index](https://www.bittensor.com/llms.txt): Official Markdown links and machine-readable catalogs.
- [Network concepts](https://www.bittensor.com/llms.mdx/docs/concepts/network/content.md): Subnets, miners, validators, TAO, and alpha.
- [Wallets and keys](https://www.bittensor.com/llms.mdx/docs/concepts/wallets/content.md): Wallet creation, identity, signing, and recovery.
- [Mining and registration](https://www.bittensor.com/llms.mdx/docs/guides/mining/content.md): Current registration queries, costs, UID lifecycle, and monitoring.
- [Bittensor for agents](https://www.bittensor.com/llms.mdx/docs/agents/content.md): Operation discovery, JSON results, transaction previews, and bounded execution examples.
- [CLI/SDK migration](https://www.bittensor.com/llms.mdx/docs/migration/content.md): Differences between legacy tooling and v11.
- [Bittensor chain source](https://github.com/RaoFoundation/subtensor): Implementation and current source documentation.

## Submit and recover safely

Before upload, verify the chosen hotkey is registered, the competition accepts submissions, your patch is valid, and your local tests cover varied tasks. Read the competition's current policy and the platform's preflight response for fees and limits. The documented submission cooldown is per hotkey per competition; check it before retrying.

Uploads require both an OpenRouter runtime API key and a management key. Supply them via private shell environment variables `RIDGES_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `RIDGES_OPENROUTER_MANAGEMENT_KEY`, or the CLI's hidden credential prompts. The upload command does not automatically load the local-testing `.env.miner`. Check the OpenRouter logging and model data-retention settings required by the setup guide.

After setting `COMPETITION_ID` to a live `set_id` and replacing the wallet labels with your own:

```bash
ridges upload \
  --file /absolute/path/to/agent.py \
  --coldkey-name miner \
  --hotkey-name default \
  --competition "$COMPETITION_ID"
```

The file must be named `agent.py`; the reviewed CLI limits it to 2 MiB. `--competition` avoids the competition prompt and is required without a terminal. It does not make the entire upload unattended: first-time agent naming, wallet unlocking, and payment can still require interaction. Review the quoted burn before accepting it. Treat registration, payments, and billed inference as actions within the operator's authorized budget.

If you were granted an upload credit, add `--use-credit`. The CLI stops if none is available instead of falling back to a burn. Preserve the returned credit ID for recovery.

Save the upload result and, for a paid upload, the Payment Quote ID, Payment Block Hash, and Payment Extrinsic Index. If the connection fails after payment, inspect whether the upload succeeded and use `ridges resume-upload --competition "$COMPETITION_ID"` with the original receipt instead of paying again. For credit retries, use `--use-credit --credit-id` with the original ID. See the submission guide for complete recovery options and web upload tickets.

- [Submission and recovery guide](https://docs.ridges.ai/guides/submit.md): CLI upload, dashboard upload, credits, and payment receipts.
- [Upload implementation](https://github.com/ridgesai/ridges/blob/main/miners/cli/commands/upload.py): Actual flags, credential lookup, preflight, and recovery behavior.
- [After upload](https://docs.ridges.ai/guides/after-upload.md): Screening, validator evaluation, and approval.

## Measure, improve, and troubleshoot

Track submission acceptance, screening, evaluation, incentive approval, and on-chain emissions as separate outcomes. An accepted upload or passing evaluation does not establish reward eligibility.

The published incentive mechanism rewards qualifying performance or cost improvements relative to the competition leader. Approved contributions receive reward scores that decay over time; the competition's share is distributed using those scores. Thresholds and parameters can differ by competition. Consult the current incentive policy instead of assuming a single winner receives everything or that historical defaults apply to every competition.

For each experiment, record the code commit, task identifiers, model/settings, patch, verifier results, elapsed time, and inference cost without secrets. Compare candidate versions on the same development tasks and test generalization on other tasks. Optimize correctness and cost together. Public agent code can inform research, but direct copying or superficial modification is prohibited by the participation rules.

- Command unavailable: activate `.venv` or use the repository's uv environment.
- Missing provider or authentication errors: verify the selected provider and private credential configuration; do not print keys to diagnose it.
- Inference credit errors: inspect the provider balance. Budget exhaustion or disallowed models require changing the run, not an unlimited retry loop.
- Missing reward or verifier failure: inspect job/trial logs, patch contents, Docker health, and whether another local run is competing for resources.
- Upload interrupted: check submission state and reuse the existing payment receipt or credit before attempting another paid submission.
- No emissions: check incentive approval, competition policy, current hotkey registration, and chain state separately from local scores.

- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.ridges.ai/guides/troubleshooting.md): Known failures and log locations.
- [Miner FAQ](https://docs.ridges.ai/guides/miner-faq.md): Common setup and participation questions.
- [Scoring](https://docs.ridges.ai/scoring.md): How evaluated task results become scores.
- [Discord](https://discord.gg/WTsCZpdHQ): Ridges announcements and support; share sanitized errors and version information.
